canonical.title: Styling engine and Tailwind 4 interop: which React component kit survives the cascade

parent.title: Which React UI component kit should itenium-ui adopt in 2026?

siblings.title: MUI vs shadcn/ui vs Mantine vs Base UI: the 2026 maturity and governance baseline
siblings.summary: The four kits are not the same category: MUI and Mantine are batteries-included libraries, shadcn/ui is a code registry, Base UI is primitives — and as of July 2026 shadcn/ui defaults to Base UI, making MUI's own primitive layer the de-facto industry standard.

siblings.title: Admin-console component coverage: what MUI, shadcn/ui, Mantine and Base UI actually ship in 2026
siblings.summary: Only Mantine covers a CRUD admin console in-box with a single gap (the data grid); MUI's coverage is real but the grid features you actually need are paywalled; shadcn now defaults to Base UI, making them one choice, not two.

siblings.title: A11y & primitive foundations: what MUI, shadcn/ui, Mantine and Base UI actually inherit in 2026
siblings.summary: shadcn-vs-Base-UI is a false dichotomy: since July 2026 shadcn/ui ships Base UI as its default primitive layer, so the real choice is which primitive foundation you inherit — and none of the four kits publishes a VPAT.

siblings.title: Theming, tokens and brand reach: MUI vs shadcn/ui vs Mantine vs Base UI in 2026
siblings.summary: On a Tailwind-4 monorepo the token substrate decides the kit: shadcn/ui and Base UI put brand tokens directly in @theme, while MUI and Mantine keep a JS theme object as the source of truth and only emit CSS variables downstream.

siblings.title: Nx 21 build ergonomics: which UI kit survives a shared itenium-ui library
siblings.summary: shadcn/ui's copy-in model does work in a shared Nx library, but only if you own the plumbing: a components.json in the lib, a private registry for updates, and Tailwind 4 @source globs across the boundary.

sources.title: https://github.com/mui/pigment-css
sources.claim: The Pigment CSS repo itself declares the project is in alpha and on hold, though it is not archived (1,124 stars, 148 open issues, last push 2026-06-06).

sources.title: https://mui.com/blog/2026-and-beyond/
sources.claim: MUI officially stated on 1 Jan 2026 that Pigment CSS development is paused and that resources were redirected to Base UI.

sources.title: https://mui.com/blog/introducing-material-ui-v9/
sources.claim: Material UI v9 shipped 8 Apr 2026 still on Emotion; removing the Emotion dependency is listed only under 'What's next', and the release claims ~3% bundle reduction vs v7 and up to 30% faster sx.

sources.title: https://registry.npmjs.org/@mui/material
sources.claim: The latest Material UI stable is 9.2.0 (3 Jul 2026); MUI skipped v8 entirely, going 7.0.0 (26 Mar 2025) straight to 9.0.0 (7 Apr 2026), and Emotion is an optional peer dependency alongside an optional @mui/material-pigment-css peer.

sources.title: https://registry.npmjs.org/@mui/styled-engine
sources.claim: Emotion is still the de facto runtime engine in MUI v9: @mui/styled-engine 9.1.1 hard-depends on @emotion/cache, @emotion/serialize and @emotion/sheet.

sources.title: https://github.com/mui/pigment-css/releases
sources.claim: Pigment CSS shipped v0.0.30 in Jan 2025 and then nothing for 16 months until a maintenance-only v0.0.31 on 22 May 2026; the last commit (6 Jun 2026) is an internal repo-normalization chore.

sources.title: https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/45759
sources.claim: An open MUI issue titled 'What is the way forward for styling @ mui?' (opened 30 Mar 2025) captures community frustration that v7 still ships Emotion while Pigment stalled.

sources.title: https://mui.com/material-ui/integrations/tailwindcss/tailwindcss-v4/
sources.claim: Material UI has an official, first-party Tailwind CSS v4 integration built on CSS cascade layers via enableCssLayer.

sources.title: https://mui.com/material-ui/customization/css-layers/
sources.claim: MUI's modularCssLayers option splits output into five layers (mui.global, mui.components, mui.theme, mui.custom, mui.sx); the docs do not state which version introduced it.

sources.title: https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/44700
sources.claim: MUI maintainers acknowledged that some component selectors exceed (0,1,0) specificity and that under Tailwind v4's native layers MUI could not be overridden without !important; fixed via the enableCssLayer prop (PR #45428).

sources.title: https://github.com/mui/material-ui/blob/master/skills/material-ui-tailwind/AGENTS.md
sources.claim: MUI ships an official agent skill for MUI+Tailwind that requires cssVariables: true so --mui-* tokens can be reused inside Tailwind's @theme.

sources.title: https://mui.com/material-ui/customization/css-theme-variables/usage/
sources.claim: CSS theme variables in MUI are enabled with createTheme({ cssVariables: true }) and consumed through the normal ThemeProvider.

sources.title: https://mui.com/material-ui/migration/upgrade-to-v9/
sources.claim: The v9 migration guide contains no styling-engine change: breaking changes are deprecated CSS classes, removed system props and theme component types, not a move off Emotion.

sources.title: https://base-ui.com/react/overview/releases
sources.claim: Base UI hit stable v1.0 on 11 Dec 2025, v1.1 on 15 Jan 2026 and v1.6.0 on 17 Jun 2026, and is explicitly styling-engine agnostic.

sources.title: https://github.com/mui/base-ui
sources.claim: Base UI (MUI's unstyled component library, co-maintained with Radix and Floating UI contributors) has 10,336 stars and is actively pushed (2026-07-14).

sources.title: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/changelog/2026-07-base-ui-default
sources.claim: In July 2026 shadcn/ui made Base UI its default primitive library, replacing Radix as the default (Radix still supported).

sources.title: https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/02/baseui-v1-accessible/
sources.claim: InfoQ reported (Feb 2026) that MUI released Base UI 1.0 with 35 accessible unstyled components and a long-term maintenance commitment.

sources.title: https://www.pkgpulse.com/guides/state-of-css-in-js-2026
sources.claim: Emotion downloads are flat-to-declining (10M in 2023 to 9.1M in 2026, held up mainly by MUI) while Tailwind doubled to 12M; Emotion adds ~15KB of runtime.

sources.title: https://github.com/mui/material-ui/pull/45428
sources.claim: The enableCssLayer prop was added to StyledEngineProvider by MUI maintainer siriwatknp, wiring Emotion output into @layer mui.

sources.title: https://github.com/mui/pigment-css/discussions/249
sources.claim: The 'Status of project' discussion on the Pigment CSS repo is the community's long-running thread asking for updates, with no substantive team roadmap answer beyond pointers to other threads.

sources.title: https://mui.com/material-ui/integrations/styled-components/
sources.claim: MUI documents Emotion as the default style engine, with styled-components as a swappable alternative.

sources.title: https://github.com/emotion-js/emotion
sources.claim: Emotion itself remains maintained but slow-moving (18,019 stars, last push 2026-05-06).

sources.title: https://mui.com/material-ui/guides/interoperability/
sources.claim: MUI's older style-library-interoperability guide is the Tailwind v3-era recipe: StyledEngineProvider injectFirst, preflight:false, important:'#root'/'#__next'.

sources.title: https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/45096
sources.claim: Jan 2025 docs issue: users found Tailwind v4 utilities like m-2 silently not applying against MUI because MUI's Emotion CSS is unlayered while utilities sit in @layer utilities; closed as duplicate of #44700.

sources.title: https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/discussions/20306
sources.claim: July 2026 Tailwind discussion on specificity wars with third-party component libraries: unlayered CSS beats layered CSS regardless of specificity; MUI v6+ can opt into a layer, raw Emotion/styled-components cannot.

sources.title: https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/discussions/15466
sources.claim: Dec 2024 discussion 'Tailwind 4.0 not usable with any system that provides its own styles' — host/global unlayered styles beat v4 utilities; no maintainer answer, community workaround is to import utilities.css WITHOUT a layer.

sources.title: https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/discussions/15866
sources.claim: Tailwind v4 removed the JS `important` config option; collaborator wongjn's answer is to hand-roll layer imports instead (Jan 2025, 17 replies).

sources.title: https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/discussions/17994
sources.claim: The v4 replacement for `important: true` is the CSS-first `@import "tailwindcss" important;` (collaborator wongjn, 13 May 2025); per-utility form moved to trailing bang (bg-red-500!).

sources.title: https://tailwindcss.com/docs/upgrade-guide
sources.claim: Tailwind v4 dropped corePlugins (so `corePlugins: { preflight: false }` is gone) and moved the important modifier to the end of the class name.

sources.title: https://tailwindcss.com/docs/preflight
sources.claim: In Tailwind v4 preflight is disabled by omitting the preflight.css import, and preflight zeroes margins/padding, unstyles headings and lists, and resets borders — all of which double up with MUI CssBaseline.

sources.title: https://github.com/emotion-js/emotion/issues/3134
sources.claim: Emotion has no built-in way to wrap its generated CSS in a cascade layer; the request is still open since Nov 2023, labelled documentation/needs-triage.

sources.title: https://github.com/styled-components/styled-components/issues/3950
sources.claim: styled-components likewise lacks cascade-layer support: @layer inside a styled block emits the at-rule without the generated class selector (opened Feb 2023, closed).

sources.title: https://github.com/livewire/flux/issues/783
sources.claim: Independent confirmation of the same class of bug in another kit: runtime-injected unlayered stylesheets overwrite Tailwind v4 utilities because unlayered declarations outrank layered ones.

sources.title: https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/discussions/11464
sources.claim: Long-running community thread on MUI+Tailwind (2023-2024): Tailwind classes appear not to apply at all next to MUI; advice was prefix + important config flags, or 'use a Tailwind-native kit instead'.

sources.title: https://dev.to/shankarjatin/when-tailwind-breaks-in-production-how-environment-differences-material-ui-style-conflicts-1p64
sources.claim: Shipped-app postmortem (28 Jul 2025): MUI Emotion styles outranked Tailwind utilities in production; fix was to pick one system per concern and use Tailwind v4 layers.

sources.title: https://infinum.com/handbook/frontend/react/tailwind/best-practices
sources.claim: Steelman: Infinum's engineering handbook treats Tailwind + MUI coexistence as a supported pattern (Tailwind for layout, MUI theme for stateful styles) provided import order and CSS-variable theming are set up.

sources.title: https://medium.com/@kazzywiz7/the-tailwind-v4-css-rule-that-silently-overrides-your-utilities-d72e185627ac
sources.claim: Explainer (16 Apr 2026) of the v4 cascade rule that bites CSS-in-JS: anything outside @layer sits above every named layer and always wins.

sources.title: https://dev.to/wafa_bergaoui/tailwind-css-vs-mui-vs-ant-design-which-one-should-you-choose-in-2026-3pjb
sources.claim: Feb 2026 comparison frames Tailwind and MUI as competing philosophies rather than complements; specificity conflicts cited as a scale problem.

sources.title: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/tailwind-v4
sources.claim: shadcn/ui's official Tailwind v4 page documents the CSS-first migration: tailwind.config.js dropped in favour of @theme inline, HSL colours converted to OKLCH, tailwindcss-animate deprecated for tw-animate-css, data-slot on every primitive, forwardRef removed for React 19.

sources.title: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/changelog
sources.claim: shadcn/ui 2025-2026 changelog: Tailwind v4 support (Feb 2025), React 19 + Sidebar (Oct 2024/2025), monorepo support (Dec 2024/2025), CLI 3.0 + MCP (Aug 2025), CLI v4 (Mar 2026), unified radix-ui package (Feb 2026), shadcn eject (May 2026), GitHub registries (Jun 2026), Base UI default (Jul 2026).

sources.title: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/changelog/2026-03-cli-v4
sources.claim: shadcn CLI v4 (March 2026) adds --dry-run/--diff/--view inspection flags, `shadcn info`, `shadcn docs`, presets via `init --preset`, `--monorepo` scaffolding, `--base` to pick Radix or Base UI, and registry:base to distribute a whole design system in one install.

sources.title: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/changelog/2026-02-radix-ui
sources.claim: February 2026: shadcn components moved from dozens of @radix-ui/react-* packages to the single unified `radix-ui` package, migratable with `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest migrate radix`.

sources.title: https://github.com/dcastil/tailwind-merge/blob/main/docs/changelog/v2-to-v3-migration.md
sources.claim: tailwind-merge v3 drops Tailwind v3 support and adds Tailwind v4 support; theme scales were renamed to the v4 theme-variable namespaces, custom separators removed, prefix syntax changed from 'tw-' to 'tw', validators.isLength removed - so tailwind-merge v2 + Tailwind v4 mis-resolves class conflicts.

sources.title: https://github.com/dcastil/tailwind-merge
sources.claim: tailwind-merge is at v3.6.0 (published 2026-05-10), supports Tailwind v4.0-v4.3, and users on Tailwind v3 must stay on tailwind-merge v2.6.x; the repo has 5,653 stars and 28 open issues (last push 2026-07-13).

sources.title: https://registry.npmjs.org/shadcn
sources.claim: The shadcn CLI npm package is at 4.13.0, published 2026-07-03 (canary 4.2.0-canary.0, rc 4.10.0-rc).

sources.title: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shadcn-ui/ui/main/apps/v4/registry/new-york-v4/lib/utils.ts
sources.claim: shadcn's cn() helper is literally twMerge(clsx(inputs)) - clsx for conditional class composition plus tailwind-merge for last-wins conflict resolution.

sources.title: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shadcn-ui/ui/main/apps/v4/registry/new-york-v4/ui/button.tsx
sources.claim: As of July 2026 the shadcn Button still uses class-variance-authority (cva) for variants, imports Slot from the unified `radix-ui` package, and uses the Tailwind v4 size-* utility (e.g. size-9, size-4) instead of paired w-*/h-*.

sources.title: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shadcn-ui/ui/main/apps/v4/package.json
sources.claim: shadcn/ui's own v4 app pins react 19.2.3, @base-ui/react 1.6.0, radix-ui ^1.4.3, tailwind-merge ^3.6.0, class-variance-authority ^0.7.1, clsx ^2.1.1, @tailwindcss/postcss ^4.3.0 - i.e. cva 0.7.1 is still the production dependency.

sources.title: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shadcn-ui/ui/main/apps/v4/app/globals.css
sources.claim: shadcn's Tailwind v4 stylesheet uses @import "tailwindcss"; @import "tw-animate-css"; @import "shadcn/tailwind.css"; @custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *)); and an @theme inline block mapping --color-* to bare CSS vars.

sources.title: https://registry.npmjs.org/class-variance-authority
sources.claim: class-variance-authority's last stable release is 0.7.1, published 2024-11-26 - roughly 20 months without a release as of July 2026 - while its successor package `cva` sits at 1.0.0-beta.7 (published 2026-07-13), still beta after 2+ years.

sources.title: https://registry.npmjs.org/tailwind-variants
sources.claim: tailwind-variants (the main cva alternative, from HeroUI) is at 3.2.2, published 2025-11-22, and offers slots/compound-slots plus built-in tailwind-merge.

sources.title: https://registry.npmjs.org/tailwindcss
sources.claim: Tailwind CSS latest is 4.3.2 (2026-06-29); the v3 line is frozen at 3.4.19 under the v3-lts tag (2025-12-10).

sources.title: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components-json
sources.claim: components.json's tailwind.config field must be left blank for Tailwind v4; tailwind.cssVariables and tailwind.baseColor cannot be changed after init.

sources.title: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/installation/vite
sources.claim: Vite + Tailwind v4 + shadcn wiring needs @tailwindcss/vite in vite.config plugins, an '@' -> ./src resolve alias, and matching baseUrl/paths in BOTH tsconfig.json and tsconfig.app.json; no PostCSS config and no tailwind.config.ts.

sources.title: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/monorepo
sources.claim: shadcn monorepo support uses Turborepo with apps/web + packages/ui, a components.json per workspace (style/iconLibrary/baseColor must match), globals.css centralised in packages/ui/src/styles, and imports via @workspace/ui/components.

sources.title: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/mcp
sources.claim: The shadcn MCP server lets agents browse/search/install registry items in natural language and works with the public registry, third-party registries, and authenticated private registries.

sources.title: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/registry/namespace
sources.claim: Namespaced registries are configured in components.json under `registries` with a {name} URL template and optional auth headers; the system is decentralised with no central registrar, so teams can host internal design systems.

sources.title: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48791328
sources.claim: The HN thread on shadcn defaulting to Base UI (2026-07-05, 282 points) shows a live split over the copy-in model: critics call it churn and non-differentiating, defenders cite MUI v4->v5 upgrade hell.

sources.title: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46690996
sources.claim: A January 2026 HN comment captures the anti-shadcn position: over-complex Radix-derived components (radio, select) and a leaner non-shadcn POC.

sources.title: https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/issues/6920
sources.claim: shadcn-ui/ui issue #6920 (opened 2025-03-13, closed as not planned) is a representative Tailwind v4 theme-migration complaint: the OKLCH + @theme inline token change visually broke custom themes.

sources.title: https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/discussions/6797
sources.claim: shadcn-ui/ui discussion #6797 documents the common Vite + Tailwind v4 + shadcn failure mode where component styling 'looks weird' after install, typically from stale tailwind.config/PostCSS setup or an unmigrated globals.css.

sources.title: https://zippystarter.com/blog/guides/migrating-tailwind3-to-tailwind4-with-shadcn
sources.claim: A v3->v4 shadcn migration write-up lists the concrete breakage: renamed utilities (shadow-sm->shadow-xs, rounded-sm->rounded-xs, ring->ring-3, outline-none->outline-hidden), removed *-opacity-* utilities, tailwindcss-animate -> tw-animate-css, tailwind-merge bump, Vite projects must switch to @tailwindcss/vite and can delete postcss.config.js.

sources.title: https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui
sources.claim: shadcn-ui/ui has 119,064 stars and 2,108 open issues (last push 2026-07-13) - by far the largest React UI repo, but with a large open-issue backlog.

sources.title: https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives
sources.claim: Radix Primitives remains actively maintained (19,064 stars, pushed 2026-07-13, 339 open issues) and the unified radix-ui package shipped 1.6.2 on 2026-07-06, so a Radix-based shadcn install is not abandonware.

sources.title: https://github.com/joe-bell/cva
sources.claim: class-variance-authority's repo (joe-bell/cva) has 6,856 stars and only 4 open issues, with active pushes (2026-07-13) despite the stable release being 20 months old - development has shifted to the cva 1.0 beta line.

sources.title: https://registry.npmjs.org/@mantine/core
sources.claim: The latest Mantine release on npm as of 2026-07-14 is @mantine/core 9.4.1, published 2026-06-28.

sources.title: https://mantine.dev/changelog/9-0-0/
sources.claim: Mantine 9.0.0 shipped on March 31, 2026; it is a feature/theming release (defaultRadius sm->md, fontWeights theme key) with no rework of the CSS-modules/PostCSS styling architecture.

sources.title: https://mantine.dev/guides/8x-to-9x/
sources.claim: The 8.x->9.x migration guide lists no breaking changes to the PostCSS preset or cascade layers; the styling breaking change is that `light` variant CSS variables became solid colors instead of transparent.

sources.title: https://mantine.dev/styles/mantine-styles/
sources.claim: Every Mantine package that ships CSS also ships a parallel `styles.layer.css` in which all rules are wrapped in `@layer mantine`, making Mantine overridable regardless of import order.

sources.title: https://mantine.dev/styles/global-styles/
sources.claim: `@mantine/core/styles.css` includes a minimal CSS reset (body margin 0, box-sizing border-box, font inheritance on form elements) plus :root/body styles and static utility classes, so it collides with Tailwind Preflight.

sources.title: https://mantine.dev/styles/postcss-preset/
sources.claim: postcss-preset-mantine supplies the light-dark(), rem()/em() functions and @mixin hover / smaller-than / larger-than mixins used in Mantine CSS modules, and is explicitly optional, not required.

sources.title: https://registry.npmjs.org/postcss-preset-mantine
sources.claim: postcss-preset-mantine is at 1.18.0, last published 2025-06-30 - it is stable/low-churn and shared across Mantine 7/8/9.

sources.title: https://help.mantine.dev/q/third-party-styles
sources.claim: Mantine has no dedicated 'Usage with Tailwind' docs page; the official FAQ answer is to disable Tailwind preflight, otherwise follow a community GitHub discussion.

sources.title: https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/discussions/15832
sources.claim: In Tailwind v4 all utilities live inside cascade layers, so unlayered Mantine `styles.css` rules beat Tailwind utilities - the exact regression vs v3 that users hit with Mantine.

sources.title: https://github.com/orgs/mantinedev/discussions/7459
sources.claim: The canonical Mantine+Tailwind4 discussion (opened 2025-02-06): the v3 recipe (corePlugins.preflight:false + @layer tailwind) is dead; top-voted fix is declaring `@layer theme, base, mantine, components, utilities;` then importing tailwindcss and `@mantine/core/styles.layer.css`.

sources.title: https://github.com/Songkeys/tailwind-preset-mantine
sources.claim: tailwind-preset-mantine (176 stars, last push 2026-06-23) is a third-party Tailwind v4 preset that fixes layer order (theme -> base -> mantine -> components -> utilities) and maps Mantine theme tokens into Tailwind.

sources.title: https://registry.npmjs.org/tailwind-preset-mantine
sources.claim: tailwind-preset-mantine 4.1.0 was published 2026-06-23, i.e. the community bridge is actively maintained in 2026, but it is a single-maintainer package.

sources.title: https://medium.com/@stanykhay29/how-to-set-up-next-js-with-mantine-ui-and-tailwind-css-v4-for-ssr-safe-dark-mode-dea0a1be31b0
sources.claim: A working Next.js + Mantine + Tailwind v4 setup runs both PostCSS plugins in one postcss.config.mjs and uses the mantine cascade layer plus useComputedColorScheme for SSR-safe dark mode.

sources.title: https://mantine.dev/styles/css-variables/
sources.claim: Mantine theming is pure CSS custom properties (--mantine-color-{name}-{0..9}) generated by MantineProvider, with a cssVariablesResolver hook - so Tailwind can consume Mantine tokens via var().

sources.title: https://mantine.dev/styles/styles-api/
sources.claim: Mantine's Styles API exposes a classNames prop targeting every inner element of a component, which is the seam through which Tailwind utility classes are injected.

sources.title: https://base-ui.com/react/handbook/styling
sources.claim: Base UI ships zero CSS and prescribes no styling solution; you style via className (string or function of state), style prop, data attributes and exposed CSS variables.

sources.title: https://base-ui.com/react/overview/about
sources.claim: Base UI is built by people from Radix (Colm Tuite), Floating UI (James Nelson) and Material UI (Michał Dudak, Marija Najdova and others).

sources.title: https://base-ui.com/react/components/select
sources.claim: Select exposes state via data attributes (data-popup-open, data-open, data-closed, data-side, data-align, data-highlighted, data-selected, data-disabled, data-starting-style, data-ending-style, data-placeholder) and positioning via CSS variables --anchor-width, --anchor-height, --available-height, --available-width, --transform-origin; docs examples use CSS Modules.

sources.title: https://base-ui.com/react/components/combobox
sources.claim: Base UI Combobox is composed of 26 separately styleable parts (Root, Input, InputGroup, Chips, Chip, ChipRemove, List, Portal, Backdrop, Positioner, Popup, Arrow, Status, Empty, Collection, Row, Item, ItemIndicator, Group, GroupLabel, Separator, ...); the component list contains no Table or DataGrid.

sources.title: https://base-ui.com/react/overview/quick-start
sources.claim: Install is a single tree-shakable package (@base-ui/react, v1.6.0); no Tailwind plugin is required, styling is entirely left to the consumer.

sources.title: https://tailwindcss.com/docs/hover-focus-and-other-states
sources.claim: Tailwind 4 styles Base UI state natively: bare boolean data variants (data-active:border-purple-500) for flag attributes like data-open/data-disabled, and data-[side=top]: bracket syntax for valued attributes — no plugin needed.

sources.title: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/changelog/2026-01-base-ui
sources.claim: shadcn/ui added Base UI as a selectable primitive in December 2025 (via `npx shadcn create`) with visual parity between the Radix and Base UI builds — the Tailwind class layer is shared.

sources.title: https://www.greatfrontend.com/blog/top-headless-ui-libraries-for-react-in-2026
sources.claim: 2026 comparison: Radix, Base UI, React Aria, Ark UI and Headless UI all ship unstyled primitives; Radix updates slowed after the WorkOS acquisition and Base UI is now considered the more actively maintained primitive layer.

sources.title: https://tailkits.com/blog/base-ui-vs-shadcn-ui-vs-radix-ui-comparison/
sources.claim: Styling cost of Base UI stated bluntly: you write all the CSS for every component, there are no themes, no color schemes, no pre-built design patterns, and it requires design skill.

sources.title: https://www.shadcnblocks.com/blog/introducing-base-ui-and-component-styles
sources.claim: Third-party pre-styled Tailwind layers on Base UI exist: Shadcnblocks added Base UI support 5 Feb 2026, switchable via one line in components.json with identical Tailwind styling across both primitives.

sources.title: https://basecn.dev/docs/get-started/migrating-from-radix-ui
sources.claim: basecn.dev is a shadcn-style pre-styled Tailwind component collection built specifically on Base UI, with its own Radix-to-Base-UI migration guide.

sources.title: https://github.com/tailwindlabs/headlessui
sources.claim: Headless UI (28,663 stars) is not archived but its last push was 2026-04-13 — three months stale as of July 2026 — versus Base UI and Radix pushing daily.

sources.title: https://github.com/chakra-ui/ark
sources.claim: Ark UI (chakra-ui/ark, 5,282 stars, pushed 2026-07-13) is the multi-framework unstyled alternative; React Aria Components lives in adobe/react-spectrum (15,662 stars).

sources.title: https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum
sources.claim: React Aria Components ships from adobe/react-spectrum: 15,662 stars, 577 open issues, actively pushed 2026-07-14.

sources.title: https://base-ui.com/react/overview/releases/v1-6-0
sources.claim: v1.6.0 (18 June 2026) was bugfix-only — no new components — with a breaking rename OTPFieldPreview -> OTPField; even post-1.0 minors can carry breaking export renames.

sources.title: https://shadcnstudio.com/blog/migrate-from-radix-ui-to-base-ui/
sources.claim: Radix-to-Base-UI migration is component-by-component, not a drop-in: asChild is replaced by an explicit render prop and positioning moves to @floating-ui/react; a big-bang replacement is advised against.

sources.title: https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/blob/main/packages/tailwindcss/index.css
sources.claim: Tailwind v4's entry stylesheet is literally four lines: it declares the layer order `theme, base, components, utilities` and imports theme.css into `theme`, preflight.css into `base`, and utilities.css into `utilities`.

sources.title: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@layer
sources.claim: Per the CSS cascade spec, normal (non-!important) unlayered author styles always beat normal declarations inside any cascade layer, irrespective of specificity or source order; !important reverses this.

sources.title: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@import
sources.claim: `@import url layer(layer-name)` assigns an entire third-party stylesheet into a named cascade layer, which is the mechanism for taming unlayered vendor CSS.

sources.title: https://tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwindcss-v4
sources.claim: Tailwind v4 deliberately builds on native cascade layers and ships a first-party Vite plugin; benchmark full build 378ms (v3.4) -> 100ms (v4), incremental with new CSS 44ms -> 5ms, incremental with no new CSS 35ms -> 192 microseconds.

sources.title: https://tailwindcss.com/docs/adding-custom-styles
sources.claim: The `@utility` directive registers custom utilities into the built-in `utilities` layer (so they get variant support and correct sort order); `@layer base` and `@layer components` remain the way to add resets and overridable component classes.

sources.title: https://tailwindcss.com/docs/styling-with-utility-classes
sources.claim: Tailwind v4 escape hatches for specificity: the `!` suffix on a single utility, and the `important` flag on the import which marks ALL utilities !important (which then also wins over unlayered third-party CSS).

sources.title: https://tailwindcss.com/docs/compatibility
sources.claim: Tailwind explicitly does NOT recommend combining CSS modules with Tailwind: each CSS module is processed separately by Vite/Parcel/Turbopack, so 50 modules means Tailwind runs 50 times, and modules have no @theme unless you add `@reference`.

sources.title: https://vite.dev/guide/features
sources.claim: Vite auto-applies any valid postcss.config.* to ALL imported CSS, independent of Vite plugins; .module.css is handled as CSS modules; Lightning CSS can replace PostCSS only via experimental css.transformer.

sources.title: https://tailwindcss.com/docs/installation/using-vite
sources.claim: @tailwindcss/vite is installed as a Vite plugin (`plugins: [tailwindcss()]`) with no postcss.config and no content globs; the alternative @tailwindcss/postcss path exists for frameworks that require PostCSS.

sources.title: https://dev.to/srmagura/why-were-breaking-up-wiht-css-in-js-4g9b
sources.claim: Measured Emotion runtime cost: a component rendering in 54.3ms with Emotion dropped to 27.7ms after removing it (~48% faster); runtime serialization recurs on every render.

sources.title: https://react.dev/reference/react/useInsertionEffect
sources.claim: React officially discourages runtime <style> tag injection (the Emotion/styled-components model): it forces frequent browser style recalculation and is unfixable; React recommends static CSS extraction plus inline styles instead.

sources.title: https://tailwindcss.com/docs/detecting-classes-in-source-files
sources.claim: Tailwind 4 auto-detects classes starting from the current working directory, skips .gitignore'd files, node_modules, binary files, CSS files and lock files; @source paths are resolved relative to the CSS file, and source(none) disables auto-detection entirely.

sources.title: https://nx.dev/docs/technologies/react/guides/using-tailwind-css-in-react
sources.claim: Nx's official React guide states Tailwind v4 auto-detection with the Vite plugin only scans the app directory, so libs must be added explicitly with @source directives such as @source "../../../libs/ui".

sources.title: https://nx.dev/blog/setup-tailwind-4-npm-workspace
sources.claim: Nx blog: with @tailwindcss/vite in an npm/pnpm workspace, styles defined in workspace packages are omitted from the bundle unless @source directives point at each package, producing missing styles and broken layouts.

sources.title: https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/issues/13136
sources.claim: tailwindlabs/tailwindcss issue #13136 (opened 7 Mar 2024, now closed) reported that v4 automatic content detection in monorepos only finds the direct package and that relative base paths did not work, prompting the explicit @source escape hatch.

sources.title: https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/discussions/18770
sources.claim: Aug 2025 discussion: a React+TS+Vite monorepo saw zero Tailwind utilities applied from a shared component library; Tailwind collaborator wongjn traced it to the library's package.json CSS exports and a missing CSS import in the consumer app, not just @source.

sources.title: https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/discussions/17905
sources.claim: Tailwind 4.1.5 monorepo discussion: utilities generated in dev but missing in production build; root causes were @source paths pointing at non-existent directories and the UI package not exporting its theme CSS via package.json exports.

sources.title: https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/discussions/15886
sources.claim: Nx + Angular Tailwind 4 upgrade thread (Jan-Apr 2025): 'Cannot apply unknown utility class: bg-white' errors, fixed by .postcssrc.json with @tailwindcss/postcss, adding @reference to component stylesheets using @apply, and switching from @nx/angular:webpack-browser to browser-esbuild.

sources.title: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/discussions/29810
sources.claim: Nx discussion #29810 (opened 30 Jan 2025): users waited months for native Tailwind v4 support while Nx 21 still generated Tailwind 3.x configs; in Feb 2026 maintainer @juristr announced Nx will disable its native Tailwind integration and point users at the official Tailwind guides plus a community sync generator.

sources.title: https://nx.dev/blog/setup-tailwind-4-angular-nx-workspace
sources.claim: Nx maintains a dedicated blog guide for wiring Tailwind v4 into an Nx workspace, reflecting that Tailwind 4 setup in Nx is now a documented manual process rather than an Nx executor feature.

sources.title: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@juristr/nx-tailwind-sync
sources.claim: @juristr/nx-tailwind-sync is an Nx sync generator that walks the Nx project graph and auto-writes @source directives for all transitive dependencies into the app's CSS; latest version 0.0.9 published 2026-02-10, sole maintainer juristr (Nx core team).

sources.title: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/installation/manual
sources.claim: shadcn/ui's manual installation now lists tw-animate-css (not tailwindcss-animate) as the required animation dependency.

sources.title: https://github.com/Wombosvideo/tw-animate-css
sources.claim: tw-animate-css is a solo-maintained MIT project by Wombosvideo (Luca Bosin): 781 stars, 13 forks, 18 open issues, created 2025-01-28, last push 2026-02-28; 90 of ~99 commits are the owner's and a breaking v2.0.0 is still pending.

sources.title: https://github.com/jamiebuilds/tailwindcss-animate
sources.claim: tailwindcss-animate (jamiebuilds) has 3,030 stars but its repo was last pushed 2024-07-28 and its last npm release 1.0.7 shipped 2023-08-28 - it is a Tailwind v3 JS plugin, unmaintained rather than formally npm-deprecated.

sources.title: https://registry.npmjs.org/tw-animate-css
sources.claim: npm registry: tw-animate-css latest is 1.4.0 published 2025-09-24 (only a canary 1.3.0-canary.35 since, 2026-02-28); single maintainer wombosvideo; ~35.5M downloads in the week of 2026-07-05, versus ~21.6M for the legacy tailwindcss-animate.

sources.title: https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/discussions/18270
sources.claim: Tailwind discussion #18270 (10 Jun 2025) quotes the official floor verbatim: Tailwind CSS v4.0 targets Safari 16.4+, Chrome 111+ and Firefox 128+, with users requesting wider browser support.

sources.title: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/128
sources.claim: Firefox 128 (released 9 July 2024) is the first Firefox to ship the CSS @property at-rule and CSS.registerProperty() by default - which is exactly why Tailwind 4's floor is Firefox 128.

sources.title: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color_value/color-mix
sources.claim: color-mix() reached Baseline 'widely available' in May 2023 (Chrome 111 / Safari 16.2 / Firefox 113), which is the origin of Tailwind 4's Chrome 111 floor.

sources.title: https://developer.chrome.com/blog/new-in-chrome-111
sources.claim: Chrome 111 (March 2023) is the release that shipped color-mix().

sources.title: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@property
sources.claim: @property became Baseline 'newly available' in July 2024, i.e. it is the newest of Tailwind 4's three hard requirements (@property, color-mix(), cascade layers) and therefore sets the browser floor.

sources.title: https://github.com/juristr/tailwind4-vite-npm-workspaces
sources.claim: Juri Strumpflohner (Nx core team) maintains a reference repo demonstrating Tailwind 4 + Vite across npm workspaces with explicit @source directives.

sources.title: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/changelog/2026-05-shadcn-eject
sources.claim: shadcn's May 2026 changelog states `init` now adds `@import "shadcn/tailwind.css"` to global CSS, that the file holds shared Tailwind utilities/custom variants, and that `shadcn eject` inlines it and removes the dependency.

sources.title: https://registry.npmjs.org/shadcn/latest
sources.claim: The npm package `shadcn` (v4.13.0, 'Add components to your apps.') genuinely exports a CSS file: its exports map contains "./tailwind.css": "./dist/tailwind.css", alongside ./registry, ./mcp, ./utils, ./icons and ./preset entrypoints.

sources.title: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/shadcn/dist/tailwind.css
sources.claim: The shipped shadcn/dist/tailwind.css is ~16 KB and contains accordion @keyframes, ~9 @custom-variant data-* variants (data-open/data-closed/data-checked/data-unchecked/data-selected/data-disabled/data-active/data-horizontal/data-vertical), a no-scrollbar utility, and scroll-fade/shimmer utilities — but NO colour tokens, NO :root/.dark blocks and NO `@custom-variant dark` definition; it only consumes `@variant dark` inside the shimmer utility.

sources.title: https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/discussions/9243
sources.claim: A 2026 community discussion titled 'Why does shadcn components suddenly depend on npm i shadcn' documents user backlash that Switch and other newer components stop working without `@import "shadcn/tailwind.css"`, which requires the `shadcn` npm package — breaking the 'copy the code, own it' premise.

sources.title: https://tailwindcss.com/docs/dark-mode
sources.claim: Tailwind v4 has no built-in class-based dark mode: you must declare a custom variant, either against a class or against a data attribute — this is the single hook every kit must be wired into.

sources.title: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mui/material-ui/master/docs/data/material/customization/css-theme-variables/configuration.md
sources.claim: MUI's colorSchemeSelector accepts 'class' (emits .light/.dark), 'data' (emits [data-light]/[data-dark]), or a custom %s selector such as '.theme-%s'; without it MUI dark mode is driven by prefers-color-scheme and cannot follow a .dark class toggle.

sources.title: https://mui.com/system/experimental-api/css-theme-variables/
sources.claim: The MUI System CSS-theme-variables API types colorSchemeSelector as `'media' | 'class' | 'data' | string`; the docs page does not state which value is the default.

sources.title: https://mui.com/material-ui/react-init-color-scheme-script/
sources.claim: MUI requires InitColorSchemeScript's `attribute` prop to match the theme's colorSchemeSelector; with attribute="class" it writes <html class="dark">, which is exactly the element Tailwind's .dark custom-variant keys off, so one toggle can drive both.

sources.title: https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/41511
sources.claim: MUI issue #41511 ('Is there any way to apply the Tailwind's `dark:` class prefix?') documents that Tailwind dark: utilities like 'bg-slate-300 dark:bg-slate-800' do not work on MUI components out of the box in a default MUI dark-mode setup.

sources.title: https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/38575
sources.claim: MUI issue #38575 reports the docs-site dark mode toggle not updating [data-mui-color-scheme] and thereby mis-styling the Tailwind demos — a concrete instance of MUI and Tailwind dark state drifting out of sync.

sources.title: https://mantine.dev/theming/color-schemes/
sources.claim: MantineProvider sets data-mantine-color-scheme on <html>; every Mantine component style keys off that attribute, and useMantineColorScheme/useComputedColorScheme are the toggle API. The attribute name is not documented as configurable (only the colorSchemeManager storage is).

sources.title: https://github.com/orgs/mantinedev/discussions/1672
sources.claim: Mantine's own discussion on using Tailwind together with Mantine warns that Tailwind's base/preflight styles conflict with Mantine components — the colour-scheme sync problem sits on top of an existing reset conflict.

sources.title: https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/discussions/6840
sources.claim: shadcn maintainers/community confirm `@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *));` in globals.css is not a shadcn invention but plain Tailwind v4 manual-dark-mode syntax; it is the single line that makes both Tailwind's dark: utilities and shadcn's .dark token block respond to the same .dark class.
